summary: Static ultrastructure exists: EMDB holds the bloodstream-form flagellum tomogram EMD-23621 (20.4 Å voxels) and three further T. brucei cryo-tomograms (EMD-45648, EMD-6748–6750), all centred on the axoneme rather than the whole membrane; TrypTag (BioImage Archive S-BIAD1866) gives protein localisations along the flagellum attachment zone. No open dataset gives whole-membrane 3D curvature, time-resolved undulation dynamics, or other flagellates with undulating membranes; EMPIAR could not be queried (all API routes 404) and IDR has no trypanosome images.
next_step: Segment the membrane sheet in EMD-23621 and the other tomograms to estimate local mean curvature where in frame; for the passive-vs-active question, high-speed video of trypanosome swimming would have to be sourced from paper supplements or newly recorded.
obstacles_confirmed: Few datasets combine ultrastructure, curvature, and dynamics.
Available tomograms center on the axoneme and paraflagellar rod, so the mean curvature of the whole undulating membrane is only partly in frame.
Trichomonas and spermatozoa with undulating membranes are outside this trypanosome archive, and static maps do not show whether the wave is actively driven.
